findings.summary: The round-1 fix's second branch (save failed, so answer 503 'unavailable') runs only after handover.end has already queued handover_changed {active:false} for the CRM, so the CRM is told 'ended' by the event and 'not ended, retry' by the response, while Redis still holds the visitor.
findings.failure: Visitor held in Redis. The CRM agent clicks 'hand back to AI'. The reads succeed, then the visitor store's SET of the ended record fails (redis TimeoutError on a stalled Redis, socket_timeout=1.0). handover.end then calls _tell_crm anyway. crm_events has its own client and its own breaker, so its RPUSH goes through, and hand_back answers 503 {result: unavailable}. The CRM's consumer (acuven_crm_demo chatbot_event_service.update_handover) stores wa_handover_active=False from the event regardless of the 503, so the CRM screen shows the visitor as back with the bot and the agent has nothing left to retry. Redis still holds handover_since, and once the 30 s offline window passes it is read again, so the bot stays silent on the visitor for up to HANDOVER_IDLE_SECONDS (86400 after C4). This is the same end state round-1 P2-1 was about (the CRM believes the visitor is not held while the bot treats them as held), reached through the fix. The new test test_a_hand_back_whose_save_fails_is_503_and_can_be_retried uses the `queue` fixture but never asserts on it, so it stays green. The console also gets a TOOL_END 'back with the bot' event for a hand-back that was reported as not done. For the 30 s window, the in-memory copy says ended, so the bot answers inbound messages. After the window it goes silent again because Redis still says held.

self_check.spec_coverage: The round-1 finding's own path (reads fail, so 503 instead of not_active) is fixed. The round-1 repro scenario is covered by test_a_visitor_store_that_cannot_be_read_is_503_not_nobody_held, which uses a dict-backed Redis raising ConnectionError on the real user_store, so it is not a tautology, and it asserts queue == []. offline() has unit tests for the healthy, failed-read and memory-only cases. The write-failure branch's test asserts the status and that a retry ends the takeover. It never looks at the queue it pulls in, so it passes while the contradictory event goes out (P2-1). Not covered and not reported: the window boundary. get() can skip Redis just before _offline_until expires and offline() can then read False, which gives not_active on a memory-only read. That window is microseconds, so I did not report it.

self_check.spec_deviation: 503 {result: unavailable} on /handback is a new answer. The contract's /handback section lists ended / not_active / 401 / 422 / 503 without a secret. Round 1 reported that the CRM maps every non-200 to CHATBOT_FAILED (502, nothing changed), so using 503 for 'store unreachable' fits the CRM's handling and I consider it justified. The unjustified part is P2-1: the 503 is given after the state-change event has gone out, so the CRM gets two answers that contradict each other.

phase2.rebuttals: 1) Not valid: 'CRM 侧把一切非 200 归 HANDOFF_FAILED、不改状态，正是要的效果'. That holds for the synchronous answer only. For the save-failure branch, the CRM's state is also written by the handover_changed event that handover.end has already queued before the second offline() check runs. update_handover stores active=False from it no matter what the response said. So in that branch 'CRM 不改状态' is false (P2-1, red in the repro). The plan's own text gives this away: for the read-failure branch it says '503、不推事件', and for the save-failure branch it drops that clause and says only '同样 503……重试即可'. 2) Not valid: '交还天然幂等，客服重试即可'. A retry only happens if the agent still sees something to retry. After the event lands, the CRM shows the visitor as back with the bot. 3) The mutation run ('只去掉「结束之后」那处 → 1 failed') shows that the second check changes the status code. It does not show that the second check is correct, because the test it kills never asserts on the queue, which is exactly where the contradiction is. 4) Valid: the read-failure branch, offline() returning False without Redis, the explanation of the 1334 vs 1332+2 gap (the main repo has a gitignored backend/.env that the worktree lacks), and calling the read-modify-save race pre-existing (task 20) and out of scope.
phase2.blind_spot: The developer writes this up as a known side note: the read-modify-save race with an inbound turn (a turn that read the record before the hand-back and saves after it writes handover_since back). I did not look at concurrency in phase 1 at all. I only followed single-request failure paths through the store. Round 1 had noted the same race read-only, so it is not new, but it shows that my review was built around the shape of the round-1 finding (store failures) and did not look at interleavings, even though the new 503 branches make the record's in-memory/Redis split a second place where interleavings matter. Beyond that, the developer admits nothing I missed. The one thing I found that they did not see (P2-1) comes from the same pattern as task 9's lesson 3: two sentences in their own write-up ('不推事件' for one branch, nothing about it for the other) that disagree, read side by side.
